title: Why Fats Solidify in Kitchen P-Traps
description: Fats, oils, and grease—collectively known as FOG—are the leading cause of kitchen sink blockages. When warm fats are rinsed down the drain, cold water rapidly lowers their temperature. This causes grease to congeal and cling to the inner walls of the P-trap and horizontal branch line. Over time, organic food debris becomes trapped in this sticky lining, gradually restricting wastewater flow until a complete blockage occurs. To protect your drainage system, scrape cookware into the solid trash before washing. Rinsing dishes with hot water and emulsifying dish detergent helps keep minor residual fats suspended long enough to clear the trap.

Bright, neutral laboratory lighting illuminates the interior of the pipe cutaway with crisp detail. Clean white tile background, soft shadows, realistic plumbing materials and fitting geometry, no text, no logos, no watermarks.
visual_story: The visual focuses on a cross-section cutaway of a kitchen P-trap beneath a sink. Viewers immediately notice a thick layer of solidified grease clinging to the bottom dip of the trap, narrowing the water channel. This demonstrates how fats build up silently inside the plumbing fixture before a complete stoppage happens, reinforcing why grease should never be poured into the sink.
